body:
Voice AI infrastructure is the set of models, connections, tools, and services that lets an AI agent listen to a call, decide what to do, take action in other systems, and answer out loud. And, with leading providers like ElevenLabs, all of this happens in a fraction of a second.

A production voice agent runs on a stack of layers that includes speech recognition, turn-taking, a large language model, orchestration, tools, knowledge retrieval, speech synthesis, telephony, and monitoring.

This guide explains the AI agent architecture behind a working voice agent. Each section converts what a layer does, why it matters in the wider infrastructure, and how ElevenAgents implements it, with Eleven v4 as the example voice layer.

## How voice AI infrastructure fits together

A voice agent turns audio into text, reasons based on that input, generates an answer, and then turns that response back into audio that the customer hears. That cascade of actions is made up by a robust stack of AI agent architecture.

Here are the main layers that contribute to voice AI infrastructure in 2026:

• Speech recognition: Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) technology converts the caller's audio into text for processing.

• Turn taking: Turn taking decides when the caller has finished and when to stop talking, allowing for more fluid, responsive conversation.

• Language model(s): Interprets the transcribed request and generates a reply, after pulling necessary context.

• Orchestration: An AI orchestration layer routes the conversation between prompts, subagents, tools, and humans.

• Tools and MCP: Connect the agent to external systems, such as CRM platforms or contact centers , to perform tasks.

• Knowledge and memory: Supply facts and caller context via Retrieval Augmented Generation .

• Speech synthesis: Uses Text to Speech to transform the text generation reply into audio.

• Transport and telephony: Carries audio between the agent and the caller.

• Guardrails, testing, and monitoring: Keeps the agent on task and measurable.

Together, these components work to create real-time conversations between AI agents and calling customers.

## Voice AI architecture diagram

The flow isn’t a straight line. ElevenAgents starts speaking after it receives “enough words and a comma” from the language model, meaning that audio begins playing before the full reply exists. Toll calls and retrieval run in the middle of a turn. Interruptions can arrive and are handled naturally by the agent while it generates speech.

## Two ways to build voice AI architecture

ElevenAgents supports two voice modes . In Custom mode, you pick the language model, the Text to Speech model, and the speech recognition settings yourself.

In Realtime mode , you select an Eleven Realtime model and ElevenLabs manages those settings for you. Eleven Realtime v1 Mini is the default and has the lowest latency and cost. Eleven Realtime v1 Max reasons before it responds, which suits more complex instructions and cases where multi-step tool use is required.

The system prompt , chosen voice, tools, attached knowledge base, and turn settings work the same in both modes. Custom mode is the better choice when you need a specific language model, a custom LLM, or a specific TTS model (for performance or latency optimization. )

## Speech recognition: Turning audio into text

Speech recognition, also called ASR or speech to text , is the first layer of the stack.

## What it does

The model transcribes the caller's audio continuously while they speak. Doing so continuously allows the rest of the pipeline to start working before the sentence ends, saving on latency. Advanced models will handle everything from thick accents and different speaking speeds to background noise.

## Why it matters for voice AI infrastructure

Transcription is arguably one of the most important layers in the stack because any errors here will permeate through the rest of the stages. Mishear a booking reference? Wrong customer record actioned. Get a medication’s name wrong? Potential disaster.

In its Trust Framework for Healthcare , ElevenLabs shows how high the stakes get with one misheard syllable: hydroxyzine versus hydralazine.

## How ElevenAgents does it

ElevenAgents uses Scribe v2 Realtime , which transcribes speech in approximately 150 ms. ElevenLabs trained it for noisy backgrounds, diverse accents, and identifiers such as names, emails, and IDs. On the FLEURS multilingual benchmark across 30 languages, ElevenLabs reported the lowest word error rate of any low-latency ASR model.

You enable it under the Advanced section of the agent configuration. In the same white paper mentioned above, ElevenLabs reports that Scribe v2 Medical leads every model on the public Eka Medical ASR benchmark at a 7.0% word error rate as of publication.

Accurate (and rapid) transcription gives the next layers the clean input they need without adding significant latency.

## Turn taking: Knowing when to speak and when to stop

Turn taking is the set of rules that decides when the agent replies and when it listens. Being able to effectively understand turns in conversation and act upon them is what separates a conversation from a legacy IVR phone menu .

## What it does

There are a few functions that a turn taking component provides to voice AI infrastructure:

• Voice activity detection (VAD): VAD classifies incoming audio as speech or silence, dozens of times per second.

• End-of-turn detection: Judges whether the caller has finished, using tone, rhythm, and word context.

• Barge-in: Lets the caller interrupt, at which point the agent stops talking to allow the user to continue.

• Backchannels: Short acknowledgments such as "yeah" that do not take the turn.

## Why it matters

A gap of about 200 ms is the typical gap between speakers in a human conversation. An agent that answers too early cuts callers off, while one that waits too long creates silences that make the call feel broken or unre
